transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-07-08
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Diego Alvarez (Redwood); Aisha Khan, Liam O'Connor, Rashida Patel, Ben Yu (Polaris Tech)

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick check-in — i think we have about 45 minutes. agenda is quality eval, quick run through results, any regressions, and next steps. diego will jump into the evals.
[00:18] Diego Alvarez: yep, cool. i'll share my screen — ummm — okay, there we go. first slide is baseline from last week, we ran the 2k prompt set across the model variants — hosted redwood api and dedicated pool with 4xA100 emulated. note: transcription may show A100 as A-one-oh-oh in notes.
[00:42] Aisha Khan: sorry can you repeat the throughput numbers? we saw a spike in latency on the dedicated run yesterday.
[00:49] Diego Alvarez: sure — baseline hosted average token latency 45ms per token; dedicated was 38ms per token under our batching config. but the regression we saw is in the intent classification micro-metric: precision dropped from 0.93 to 0.87 on the latest prompt set for the partial-match intents.
[01:07] Liam O'Connor: partial-match intents meaning when user asks multi-turn clarifying questions? we saw similar in our logs, some responses started to favor the auxiliary intent.
[01:16] Diego Alvarez: exactly. root cause hypothesis — a prompt drift after we added non-standard examples (the "marketplace" examples). we also flagged one prompt that is too leading, which increases hallucination.
[01:30] Rashida Patel: is that from the new guided prompt templates the product team added last week?
[01:34] Aisha Khan: yeah those, the so-called "marketplace" prompts.
[01:37] Diego Alvarez: correct. quick note: the auto scorer we ran weights intent precision higher than slot accuracy, that might be amplifying the shift.
[01:48] Maya Chen: quick QA — when you say auto scorer, is that the spreadsheet you shared last week or the pipeline in your repo?
[01:54] Diego Alvarez: spreadsheet and pipeline. the spreadsheet has the human-rater columns, we auto-aggregate into the pipeline. i'll update the spreadsheet to show per-prompt contributions to regression.
[02:06] Ben Yu: from security side: quick flag — any data retention on hosted inference? we need to ensure logs are not stored outside our VPC and KMS keys must be customer-managed if we move to private.
[02:18] Maya Chen: totally. Redwood supports customer-managed KMS for Private deployments; for Hosted we do short-term logs for debugging and those can be disabled. we'll send the security checklist again.
[02:29] Ben Yu: okay please send. also SOC-2 scope — we need encryption at rest and audit logs tied to SSO.
[02:36] Maya Chen: noted, will include in the security doc.
[02:39] [03:00] Diego Alvarez: back to results — i ran three scoring variants: original rubric, stricter precision-weighted rubric, and a recall-friendly rubric. stricter precision bumped precision to 0.91 but recall dropped. recall-friendly got recall to 0.88 but precision fell. tradeoffs as expected.
[03:22] Liam O'Connor: what's the business impact for us? are false positives worse than misses for Polaris?
[03:29] Rashida Patel: for support routing, false positives (wrongly routing to escalation) are more costly, so precision matters. for internal summarization, recall might be more important.
[03:40] Maya Chen: ok that helps. so let's calibrate the scorer to bias precision for routing flows. diego, can you surface which prompts are causing FP?
[03:49] Diego Alvarez: yes — prompt IDs 127, 142, and 189 have highest FP contribution. i'll mark them in the spreadsheet. also note prompt 142 has a template that mentions "assume the user means" which is too leading and encourages hallucination.
[04:02] Aisha Khan: can we add guardrails to avoid that? like a required clarifying follow-up?
[04:07] Diego Alvarez: yes, we can modify the prompt to include an explicit "if uncertain, ask to clarify" pattern. i'd also recommend a two-stage guardrail: 1) classification model signals low confidence, trigger clarification, 2) apply stricter decoding constraints — e.g., temperature 0.0 and top-p 0.7 for routing.
[04:28] Liam O'Connor: will those decoding constraints affect latency?
[04:32] Diego Alvarez: minimal, maybe a small token generation difference, but overall throughput the same. the bigger latency hit came from our KV cache eviction pattern yesterday — we saw cold cache on some long threads.
[04:44] Rashida Patel: KV cash? (laughs) i think the notes show 'KV cash' sometimes.
[04:48] Diego Alvarez: yeah transcription shows that, it's KV cache — key-value cache. we can tune TTL to keep prefixes hot for multi-turn flows.
[04:56] [08:00] Maya Chen: stepping back — action wise: diego, run 3 regression tests with updated prompts and the precision-weighted rubric on dedicated; capture tokens, latency, and token cost. aim to reproduce the precision drop and confirm fixes.
[08:12] Diego Alvarez: will do. i'll run on dedicated with our dedicated pool config, but note the dedicated pool we used in POC is slightly smaller than production; results should be comparable.
[08:21] Aisha Khan: for clarity, what's the test surface? only routing flows or multi-domain?
[08:26] Diego Alvarez: both — routing flows first, then multi-domain. i'll attach per-prompt traces.
[08:32] Ben Yu: security follow-up — if you move to Private, we need to ensure HSM-backed KMS, and the audit log retention must be 12 months. is that supported?
[08:41] Maya Chen: yes for Private we can do HSM-backed keys and extended audit retention as part of enterprise package, we'll send details.
[08:48] Liam O'Connor: one weird item: on some samples the model started inserting internal product names that we don't want surfaced to users. is there a way to scrub proprietary tokens?
[08:58] Diego Alvarez: yes, we support token-level blocklists and post-generation filters. also can add generation-time constraints to avoid mentioning internal names.
[09:06] Rashida Patel: good. also for the scoring, can we get a breakdown by customer persona? e.g., support vs billing vs sales routing.
[09:13] Diego Alvarez: yes — i'll add persona columns to the spreadsheet.
[09:16] Maya Chen: quick note on guardrails — we also have Redwood Optimize suggestions: intelligent batching and quantization profiles, but for quality eval we should keep the model in full-fp for now to avoid changes in behavior.
[09:28] Aisha Khan: agreed. keep quantization off while we diagnose.
[09:31] Diego Alvarez: noted. one other regression: on the hosted run we saw an edge-case where the model overwrote slot values in multi-turn. hypothesis is improper KV cache invalidation on slot reset.
[09:42] Liam O'Connor: we observed that in a thread where user updated preference mid-conversation.
[09:46] Diego Alvarez: yeah. mitigation: explicit slot-clear prompt before slot capture, and adjust KV eviction policy. i'll include test cases.
[09:55] [20:00] Maya Chen: okay let's recap next steps — maya to share updated scoring spreadsheet and annotated prompt set; diego runs regression tests and shares results; ben confirms security items. schedule benchmark run next week. any blockers?
[20:18] Aisha Khan: none from product side. just need the updated prompts.
[20:22] Rashida Patel: timeline looks good.
[20:25] Ben Yu: i'll check internal approvals for KMS and SOC2 scope, might need a short follow-up with legal.
[20:31] Maya Chen: great — final note, i'll send the security pack, updated spreadsheet, and proposed benchmarking time. thanks everyone.
[20:38] Liam O'Connor: thanks.
[20:40] Diego Alvarez: thanks all.
